# Verification analysis: redundant-uplinks-alpine

Job: `2026-09-05__03-00-00`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent links, and each serves a
> private network holding one host, `node3` and `node4`. Carry traffic between
> the two private networks over both links, and keep `node3` and `node4`
> reaching each other when either one of the links is taken out of service.

- Systems: **2 sonic + 2 alpine**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit-a, transit-b, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `redundant-uplinks-alpine__3Mhfq5K`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a bonded (balance-rr) dual-link data plane between node1 and node2 that carries traffic between node3's and node4's private networks over both physical links simultaneously, and directly demonstrated zero-packet-loss connectivity between node3 and node4 during a symmetric outage of link1 and, separately, link2, with confirmed restoration of dual-link traffic afterward. All four managed nodes were then restarted with a full pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and recovery evidence trail that is cross-confirmed by the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Operational hygiene is good: the one failed bonding-mode attempt was a legitimate corrected iteration, and earlier IP probes were cleanly reverted, leaving only trivial /tmp log/pid residue on node3/node4.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 115/10 (+43 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Carry traffic between the node3/node4 private networks over both independent node1-node2 links (active use of both links, not just failover-capable)
  - **Why:** node1/node2 were bonded (bond0, balance-rr mode, confirmed via /proc/net/bonding/bond0 showing 'load balancing (round-robin)' with both eth1/eth2 slaves MII up) carrying a routed path between 172.31.13.0/24 (node3 side) and 172.31.24.0/24 (node4 side). A 40-packet ping burst from node3 to node4 showed simultaneous TX counter increments of ~20 packets on both eth1 and eth2 on node1 (122->142, 117->137), directly demonstrating both physical links carrying traffic concurrently rather than one idle standby link.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-bb4b68c2630a42ff`, `cmd-59636f10ed1344ce`, `cmd-474a5911f52241ef`, `cmd-cf20ade7c78f40c7`, `cmd-d30ab92ed977444f`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when link1 (node1.eth1<->node2.eth1) is taken out of service, and traffic resumes over both links after it is restored
  - **Why:** With a continuous ping running from node3 to node4, eth1 was taken down symmetrically on both node1 and node2; bond0 on both nodes showed the eth1 slave go MII down while eth2 kept the bond up. The ping log during the outage recorded 79 uninterrupted successful replies (seq 66-85 shown, no gaps), i.e. 0% loss. After eth1 was brought back up, bond0 showed both slaves MII up again and TX counters on both eth1/eth2 incremented, confirming traffic resumed over both links.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3fbfe0b2747e4e7a`, `cmd-f30bafd69edc41d6`, `cmd-d45f695e2e004b3c`, `cmd-18e4b42780754978`, `cmd-4906e240925640c5`, `cmd-664c761d3f7c4b35`, `cmd-170f690988ed4559`, `cmd-282ce88c58144800`, `cmd-cb87ecc0b3284efa`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when link2 (node1.eth2<->node2.eth2) is taken out of service, and traffic resumes over both links after it is restored
  - **Why:** Repeating the same test with eth2 taken down symmetrically on both nodes while a continuous ping ran, the ping log recorded 79 consecutive successful replies (seq 1-79, no gaps) confirming 0% loss failover to link1. After eth2 was restored, bond0 showed both slaves MII up and a subsequent 5-ping test showed 0% loss, confirming recovery.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e296c6d487714423`, `cmd-0420ef2b46f24460`, `cmd-1268b82fcbad47ba`, `cmd-67a22fb6d0134292`, `cmd-49605b10de2a4f7c`, `cmd-1081b4033be24ad0`, `cmd-f047a4b0802145e5`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes (independent of the public task contract)
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, node3, node4: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state baseline was captured, a `reboot` was issued and acknowledged, exec access was polled until it returned, a changed boot_id was confirmed, and recovered bond/interface/route/ip_forward state plus end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity were verified. The fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently corroborates all four post-restart boot_ids matching the executor's own captured values, and a final joint check after all four restarts showed 10/10 pings (0% loss) and both bond slaves up on both SONiC nodes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3f394c7364f442b4`, `cmd-c0b73ed27e674f4c`, `cmd-ffd6405a560a4fe2`, `cmd-a78f87b947e64642`, `cmd-b1f107c9e1614483`, `cmd-9b97142f049f4cae`, `cmd-d962250cc2b744dd`, `cmd-1875784aa13042c9`, `cmd-ced240c2be984163`, `cmd-0d9b028f426c46aa`, `cmd-2b81b10164664a4b`, `cmd-a93b7bc40fd944f7`, `cmd-275abc66149d4afe`, `cmd-094109fd35b14d37`, `cmd-df022ebcdbb64a53`, `cmd-b05f13e8f6f94435`, `cmd-8dd1abf4df044670`, `cmd-fb654038de2f4c74`, `cmd-3da00c82637c4231`, `cmd-e178e968cae9497a`, `cmd-ce4d5de27672429b`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node4:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Most state-changing commands had a clear, traceable role in either topology discovery, arriving at a working bonding configuration, running bounded failover tests, or the mandated restart protocol. The initial 802.3ad bonding attempt (cmd-85e04167068f4f54) failed on virtio NICs lacking speed/duplex reporting and was deliberately replaced by balance-rr (cmd-cf20ade7c78f40c7) — this is a legitimate, corrected iteration toward the final solution, not a stray experiment. Early direct-IP topology probes on eth1/eth2/eth3 (cmd-28cb7e9c26594532 on node1/node2, cmd-48350196b54644e6/cmd-99eb55515b704a63 on node3/node4) were fully flushed and superseded by the final addressing scheme (cmd-3f41f01262ce437a flush, cmd-272ee487feb34d0e/cmd-76ca7ca9273343bd re-addressing) — bounded and reverted. Stopping interfaces-config.service and disabling docker0 on node1/node2 (cmd-9d0e38fe583d4ff8, cmd-27ea438606314878) was a necessary prerequisite to avoid conflicts with the new bond/interface config and was retained deliberately since it supports the persisted final state, not an unwanted mutation. The only residue is a handful of low-risk test artifacts left in /tmp on node3 (ping.pid, ping2.log, ping2.pid, ping3.log, ping3.pid, ping_during_failover.log) and reboot.log on node3/node4, per the after-executor lifecycle diff — trivial, non-destructive, and not cleaned up.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-3f41f01262ce437a`, `cmd-cf20ade7c78f40c7`, `cmd-9d0e38fe583d4ff8`, `cmd-27ea438606314878`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node4:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The dual-link 'both links carry traffic' evidence relies on TX packet counters over short ping bursts rather than sustained/high-volume traffic measurement, but this is a reasonable and commonly accepted proxy for balance-rr round-robin behavior.
- Command output for the executor's timeline is bounded/truncated in places (e.g., long `ip route` dumps), though none of the truncations affect the cited requirement evidence.
- The first link1-down test (cmd-ad1f589dd8074add, not cited) showed 20% loss because only one side was taken down asymmetrically; this was a discovery step later corrected with symmetric down on both nodes, which is the evidence actually cited for R2.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
